rationale:
ROUND 3 of the allow_reinstall trail (b8e341b9). Rounds 1 and 2 are ALREADY LIVE — chassis v1.0.1290, build stamp fa078ab3d, binary-probed on both replicas with a bogus-sha control absent, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor a36cbc6cb fa078ab3d` true. This round is small on purpose: it answers round 2's objections, and it does NOT restate shipped code as new edits, which is what drew the editquality objection to round 2's edit 1/7 overlap.

WHY THE FLAG EXISTS. install_site_composition loud-failed on any site that already had a style_collection_id, so the platform could COMPOSE a site that had nothing and could not RE-COMPOSE one that had the wrong thing. The only repair was an operator nulling sites.style_collection_id by hand, which leaves the site uncomposed until the re-resolve lands; anything rendering in that window hits the composition loader's emergency fallback (render_css_composition_loader.go:144-158) and can deploy a standard-brochure stylesheet over a live site. With the flag the swap happens inside the action's existing transaction and that window never opens.

WHAT ROUND 2's CORE OBJECTION WAS, AND WHY IT IS NOW SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN ARGUMENT. Five seats (editquality high, guardian, debug_historian, reuse_agent, prior_art_librarian) said the same thing in different words: the per-request channel reads collected_data.input_data.spec, that is a SHAPE GUESS on a documented envelope-unwrap fault line, and the plan's own risks section admitted it was unmeasured — so the round-2 fix might be as inert as round 1's. That objection was correct to raise and it has now been measured three ways, each of which could have come out otherwise:
  (1) SHAPE CENSUS, 30 days of orchestration_states carrying input_data (n=6,397): `input_data.spec` present on 2,363 runs; `input_data.body.spec` present on ZERO. The second branch the round-2 code carried was dormant machinery and is deleted in this round.
  (2) THE EXACT DISPATCH PATH, live: the two most recent needs_composition -> site-design-planner orchestrations (loancash.co.uk, cookly.uk, 2026-08-11) carry the work item's spec VERBATIM under input_data.spec — including its null-valued `planned_name` key, which is what shows the dispatcher passes the spec whole rather than projecting a named subset. Had input_mapping been an allow-list filtering this step, that null key is exactly what would have been dropped.
  (3) BEHAVIOURAL PROOF ON THE REAL CASE, 2026-08-12 13:50:13Z: work item 57b9b3ff carrying spec.allow_reinstall=true re-composed ai-agent-orchestration.com off the shared LIGHT seed collection. The site went from style_collection_id 3196d966 (shared seed `professional-dark`, palette supplies card_bg #ffffff) to a0f1ac70 with its own palette (origin=adopted, source_domain=ai-agent-orchestration.com, supplies_card_bg=FALSE). The refusal is the DEFAULT and the step config for site-design-planner's install step holds only four path references and no allow_reinstall key — so a successful install on a site that already had a collection is only reachable if the flag arrived through the work item's spec. The served artefact then moved: --color-card-bg #ffffff -> #0D1117, styles.css last-modified 2026-08-11T16:22:21Z -> 2026-08-12T13:56:26Z.

OBJECTIONS ANSWERED WITHOUT A CODE CHANGE, AND WHY.
  * bug_historian, edit 2 (RowsAffected): the check is ALREADY in the file and has been since round 1 — install_site_composition_action.go:394-409 reads RowsAffected, and on 0 aborts with a loud Error naming the site and our collection id, inside the transaction so the theme and collection inserts roll back. The seat could not see it because round 2's SKETCH stopped at the UPDATE. That is a submission defect, not a code defect; the sketch below now carries the check. No behaviour change is proposed.
  * prior_art_librarian, missing item (was the allow_reinstall census actually queried, or asserted from memory?): queried live today, and the answer has CHANGED since round 2, which is why the seat was right to ask. Active agent_definitions naming allow_reinstall: 0. Work items naming it: 1, set true — item 57b9b3ff, the ai-agent-orchestration.com repair above. So the RFC_022 scope test no longer reads 'zero live consumers'; it reads 'one, deliberate, single-site, and named here'. Stated rather than argued: the seats should judge whether one consumer changes the scope answer.
  * improvement_guardian, edit 6 (high) — the detected -> triaged change on check_integrity.go's MissingStyleCollectionCheck. The seat's reading is that discovery findings insert at `detected` so a triager promotes them deliberately, and that matching the discovery check to emit_design_items' `triaged` bypasses that gate; its recommended fix is the opposite one, making emit_design_items emit `detected`. Two facts bear on this and neither was in front of the seat. FIRST, the gate it protects is not operative: the only thing that promotes detected -> triaged is TriageDetectedItemsAction, and its three callers (improvement-loop, design-audit-agent, site-review-agent) have no enabled scheduled task between them, so `detected` today means 'stranded', not 'awaiting a human'. SECOND, since the change shipped, two discovery-produced needs_composition items (created_by design-discovery-agent, source discovery) were claimed and ran to complete — the loancash.co.uk and cookly.uk runs cited above. The seat's recommended direction would therefore strand BOTH producers rather than restore a gate. We are NOT proposing to widen this further, and we agree the underlying question — whether build-pipeline discovery findings should be human-gated at all, and by what — is real and larger than this bug. It is left explicitly open, unresolved, and named in the risks below rather than settled inside a bug patch.

WHAT THIS ROUND ACTUALLY CHANGES: three edits, all narrowing. The bespoke envelope unwrapper is replaced by the platform's existing exact-path reader, its dormant second branch is deleted, and the silent no-op the guardian seat asked about becomes diagnosable AND test-enforced.

plan.summary: Round 3, answering council b8e341b9 round 2 (REVISE). Replace the hand-rolled collected_data unwrapper with the platform's exact-path reader and delete its measured-dormant second branch; add the resolved_from diagnostic the guardian seat made its approve conditional on; add a test that fails if the two silent-no-op cases stop being distinguishable. No change to the guard, the transaction, or the default.

edits.rationale: Answers reuse_agent and prior_art_librarian (both medium, edit 8): a new bespoke two-branch unwrapper for input_data sits exactly on the documented envelope-unwrap fault line (extractContentWithFallbacks 'leaks a transport envelope by TWO branches'; page-content-writer's extractSiteID). Both seats were right that no search for an existing extractor was shown. Two exist. We use input_contracts.GetValueAtExactPath, NOT datahelpers.ExtractNestedField, and the choice is deliberate: ExtractNestedField auto-unwraps through a `.response` envelope (data_helpers.go:1248-1253), which is correct for reading data and wrong for an AUTHORITY switch — it would make the flag satisfiable by a `true` that arrived inside some other agent's reply. GetValueAtExactPath is the platform's exact-path reader with no fallbacks and no hunting (input_mapping.go:213-241). The `input_data.body.spec` branch is DELETED as dormant machinery: 0 occurrences in 30 days against 2,363 for input_data.spec. The function now also returns the path it resolved at, so the caller's log line can quote it.

Answers guardian (medium), which made its approve explicitly conditional: 'ship this with a log line naming which branch resolved the flag so a silent no-op is diagnosable, not just safe'. The seat is right about the mechanism. GetBoolFieldLoud is deliberately SILENT when a key is absent (declared_bool.go:72-75) — correct for that helper, but it means 'the spec never arrived' and 'the spec arrived without the key' produce identical logs and identical behaviour, while having completely different fixes (a dispatch/shape problem versus whoever queued the item forgot the key). resolvedFrom names which of the four cases actually decided the flag, and is logged at Info on every run, not only on the permissive branch. No control-flow change: the guard, the transaction and the default-false are untouched.

Makes the guardian's ask ENFORCED rather than merely present — a doc comment is not an enforcement mechanism, and a log line added to satisfy a reviewer is exactly the kind of thing a later edit quietly collapses. Table test over the two silent-no-op cases (no spec reached the action; spec arrived declaring nothing), asserting via zaptest/observer that resolved_from distinguishes them. Both cases still refuse, and the test asserts that too, so it cannot pass by the guard breaking. Three mutations were RUN before commit and each failed exactly one test: spec path -> 'input_data.NOPE' fails D alone; allowReinstall=false after the step-config read fails B alone; collapsing both silent-no-op strings to 'default(false)' fails F alone (both sub-cases). Each mutation hitting one test is the evidence that the three channels are independently load-bearing rather than one check wearing three names.

GetValueAtExactPath has no such branch.]

plan.risks:
RISK: Deleting the input_data.body.spec branch means a dispatch path that DOES wrap its request would stop delivering the flag.
MITIGATION: Measured at 0 occurrences in 30 days (n=6,397) against 2,363 for the kept path, so this removes machinery nothing exercises. If a third shape ever appears the action refuses (the SAFE direction, unchanged) and the new resolved_from line names the exact path it looked at — turning what would have been a silent inert flag into a one-grep diagnosis.

RISK: The detected -> triaged change from round 1 (check_integrity.go) remains live and improvement_guardian objected to it at high severity.
MITIGATION: Not widened here and not defended as settled. Stated plainly: the triage gate it protects has no enabled driver today, so `detected` currently means stranded; and two discovery-produced needs_composition items have dispatched and completed since the change. Whether build-pipeline discovery findings should be human-gated, and by what, is a larger question than this bug and is left open rather than resolved inside a bug patch.

RISK: RFC_022 scope: the field now has one live consumer where round 2 had none.
MITIGATION: Enumerated above rather than asserted. It remains opt-in with the unsafe side default OFF and a single deliberate single-site use; the seats are invited to say whether one consumer changes the answer.
